summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and chronic back pain was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and severe back pain similar to prior episodes. She presented with hyperglycemia but no ketoacidosis and was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and pain control. Her symptoms were inconsistent and closely tied to anxiety and emotional distress. Despite extensive prior workup showing only gastritis and H. pylori, her symptoms recurred, often near discharge. Psychiatric evaluation revealed that depression and anxiety were major barriers to outpatient care adherence. She improved with supportive care, was weaned off IV medications, and tolerated a full diet. Due to the psychosocial component of her recurrent admissions, she was transitioned to a crisis center for voluntary psychiatric admission. Her insulin was adjusted to 28 units of Lantus nightly, and she was discharged on oral tramadol, continued metoclopramide, and omeprazole, with follow-up planned for H. pylori treatment and physical therapy.
